Victory, and the Future
The surrender of Japan. a little more than three months

after Germany was beaten to her knees, is a victory for
civilization not less important than the defeat of Hitlerism.

“The other self-termed “master race” has met its master!

The twin conspiracies against the peace and well-being of
the world, hatched in Germany and Japan, were alike in
spirit and in method. The Nazis and the Jap military clique
had each the same inspiration; to conquer and dominate
the world, so that a favored few, who pretended to believe
themselves superior to the rest of humanity, could live in
luxury on the toll of the great majority,

Actually, they were superior only in ruthlessness and
greed, and, for a time, in preparation and equipment.

The. Nazis boasted of “Festung Europa,” a fortress 50
strong they thought it could not be breached in 1000 years,
It was conquered after the invasion in less than one.

The Japs were slightly more modest: they were ready
for a 100 years war, they sald, Just a little more than three
years ago the first dent was-made in Jap armor, at Guadal-
canal, Since that time victory has followed victory. Some
of the victories were dearly bought, as at Tarawa, Iwo, Oki-
nawa.- But as wé rolled up the Jap defenses until the
Japanese home Islands came under the guns of the Fleet, it
became evident that the collapse of Japan was inevitable.
Then came the‘application of the most terrible of war's
weapons, the atom bomb—and then the entry of Russia.
Neither affected the outcome of the war, save by bringing
it nearer.
Japan's leaders hated to acknowledge defeat; but they
have swallowed the bitter medicine.
Japan’s dream of conquering the Aslatic continent, and
from that conquering the world, is ended. °
"The Japs are back where they were 75 years ago, when
thelr careful planning began. They .have lost the fruits
of two major wars and several minor ones—beginning with
the assault on China in 1895, ‘ They will be reduced to what
they had when Commodore Perry unfortunately waked
them from’ several millennfunfs of alumber. The crimes
of their leaders will be explated; the fangs of militarism
will be drawn,
The world is once more on ifs way to peace—a peace
that will last, if the United Nations can work together in
peace as they have in war.
The worst war the world ever saw is ended!
The task now is to see there is no “next war"—for it
would mean the end of civilization.

PEACE! VICTORY!

Japs Accept Allied Terms;
Truman Names MacArthur |
to Receive Formal Surrender

WASHINGTON, Aug. 14. (U.P.)—Japan surrendered unconditionally to-
night, bringing peace to the world after the bloodiest conflict mankind has

Peace came at 7 p.m. (4 p.m. P.W.T.) when President Truman announced
that Tokyo accepted the Allied capitulation terms with no “qualification”
and that Allied forces have been ordered to cease firing.

Gen. Douglas MacArthur, “the man who came back,” was named supreme Allied com:
mander to receive the formal Japanese surrender.
VJ-Day will not be proclaimed officially until after the instruments of surrender are
\signed—probably in two or three days.
And tonight for the first time in history Emperor Hirohito broadcast to his stricken
ipeople telling them that he had accepted the Allied terms, describing the “cruel bomb”
which the Allies had turned upon the J ap homeland and warning the People they face
“great hardships and suffering.”
World War II was'at an end, except for the formality of signing surrender documents.
